free_tier.stated: The E2B Desktop Sandbox is a hosted Ubuntu 22.04/XFCE graphical sandbox driven through the E2B Desktop SDK with VNC streaming. It has no separate price or allowance: it runs on the Hobby plan, which is $0 a month with a one-time $100 in usage credits, 10 concurrent sandboxes and up to 1 hour of continuous runtime per sandbox. Sandboxes are billed per second for provisioned CPU and RAM; sandbox disk is included at no extra cost. Some accounts are asked to verify with a one-time $5 card payment, added back as usage credits.
free_tier.notes: No Desktop-only price is published: the E2B pricing page prices sandboxes by vCPU-second and GiB-second with disk free, and the Desktop docs describe a sandbox built from the stock desktop template. The credit is one-time, not a monthly allowance; the default sandbox is 2 vCPU and 4 GiB.

per_object_cap.stated: Not an object store: a desktop sandbox is a machine with 1 to 8 vCPUs and 1 to 8 GiB of RAM, 10 GiB of sandbox disk on Hobby and 20 GiB on Pro. The stock desktop template starts at 1024x768 resolution and 96 DPI.
per_object_cap.notes: The hard cap on the hosted desktop is time, not file size: 1 hour of continuous runtime per session on Hobby.

retention.stated: A desktop sandbox is killed when its timeout expires, 5 minutes by default, and its in-memory state is lost. Setting onTimeout to pause saves the filesystem and memory; a paused sandbox has no time-to-live and is kept indefinitely until killed explicitly.
retention.notes: Paused sandboxes are not billed and do not count toward the concurrency limit.

egress.terms: No egress charge or allowance is stated: the pricing page bills CPU and RAM per second and lists Disk as Free. The Desktop SDK's Sandbox.create() takes allow_internet_access, which defaults to True, and the desktop template exposes VNC via noVNC on port 6080 and a public URL for browser viewing.

interface_detail: E2B Desktop SDK (npm i @e2b/desktop; pip install e2b-desktop) drives mouse, keyboard, screenshots and commands over a sandbox REST API; stream.start() gives a noVNC URL for browser viewing.
tooling: E2B Desktop SDK in JavaScript/TypeScript and Python, the e2b CLI, and a buildable desktop template with xdotool and scrot for programmatic control.
chaining: A desktop sandbox can be paused and resumed for a long computer-use agent loop, with checkpoints written to separate object storage because a killed desktop loses its in-memory state.

limits.value: 1 hour maximum continuous runtime per desktop sandbox on Hobby; 5-minute default timeout when none is set; resets on pause and resume
one-time USD 100 in usage credits on Hobby; vCPU USD 0.000014 per second, RAM USD 0.0000045 per GiB-second, disk free
sandbox creation rate 1 per second on Hobby; GET /sandboxes 10 requests per second per project
with no payment method on file, every project in the workspace is blocked shortly after the credits run out

limits_note: The Desktop SDK's create() accepts a timeout in seconds; the maximum a sandbox can be kept alive is 1 hour on Hobby and 24 hours on Pro.
binding_note: The 1-hour continuous runtime cap decides the hosted desktop: a computer-use loop that exceeds it must pause and resume, because the credit alone does not buy an uninterrupted multi-hour session.

identity_cost.detail: The console signup page renders 'Sign up with your email and a password or a social provider' with E-Mail, Name and Password fields; no phone or card field is part of the form. The pricing page states 'No credit card required to start' but 'Some accounts are asked to verify with a one-time $5 card payment to help prevent abuse', added back as usage credits.

reliability_note: On timeout the default action kills the sandbox and its in-memory state is lost; the noVNC/WebSocket connection is not guaranteed for more than an hour and clients must reconnect. The Desktop Sandbox is documented as launched in beta.
confidence_note: The Desktop SDK surface, timeout and internet access flag come from first-party E2B docs; the rates, credit, concurrency, session cap and card verification come from the first-party pricing and billing pages read on 2026-11-24. The signup gate is read from the console registration form the same day. No Desktop-only price is published, so this record prices the Desktop Sandbox at the Hobby sandbox rates.

extras.price_arithmetic: 2 vCPU x $0.000014/s x 3600 = $0.1008/h; 4 GiB x $0.0000045/s x 3600 = $0.0648/h; disk free; total $0.1656/h. $100 / $0.1656 = 603.9 h of default desktop time, in sessions of at most 1 hour.
